# GLG Content System — Greene Legal Group
## @thesuperlawyer | Managed by Right Girl Media

This skill is the operating brain for all content produced for Attorney Reginald A. Greene (RAG) and Greene Legal Group (GLG). It covers organic Instagram, paid ads, and compliance requirements. Apply every rule here to every piece of content — no exceptions without explicit approval from Elle/RGM.

---

## WHO WE ARE TALKING TO

**The Injured Atlantan** — the one and only avatar for all GLG content.

- Recently in a car accident, slip-and-fall, or injured by someone else's negligence
- Ages 25–55, likely Black, working-class to middle-class, Atlanta metro
- Does NOT know their rights
- Afraid the process is too complicated, too expensive, or rigged against people like them
- Scrolling Instagram

**They are NOT attorneys. They are NOT legal professionals.**

Every piece of content passes this test before it goes out: *Would this person stop scrolling and feel like this was made for them?* If no — rewrite it.

---

## THE FOUR CONTENT PILLARS

**Pillar 1: Know Your Rights** — Reach content
Educates accident victims in plain English. No jargon. No attorney-to-attorney framing.
Topics: what to say to an insurance adjuster, what not to do after an accident, how long you have to file, what "no fees unless we win" actually means, what a free case review looks like.

**Pillar 2: Proof and Results** — Conversion content
Case outcomes that build trust and drive inquiries. Blurred amounts, no client names, general case type only.
Format: Before/After carousels, outcome Reels. All check/dollar amounts = large blurred figure, warm gold light wash. Never specific numbers — ever.

**Pillar 3: The Super Lawyer Brand** — Authority and personality content
Event appearances, community involvement, recognition, milestones. Shows RAG as a real person, not just a billboard.
Topics: The Summit, Spring Soirée, speaking engagements, firm anniversaries, team moments.

**Pillar 4: Behind the Case** — Engagement content
What it feels like to have RAG in your corner. The process in human terms. What happens after you call.
Topics: "Here's what happens when you call us," "What I tell every new client on day one," "The moment the insurance company realized they were wrong."

---

## POSTING CADENCE

- **Minimum:** 3 posts/week — 1 Reel + 1 Carousel + daily Stories
- **Ideal:** 4–5 posts/week — add one extra Reel or brand moment
- Consistency beats volume. Three posts every week outperforms five posts one week and nothing the next.

---

## HOOK RULES — NON-NEGOTIABLE

Every Reel and carousel opens with a hook that creates personal stakes for the avatar. Not information. Stakes.

**Use:**
- "The insurance company offered my client [blurred]. We got them [blurred]."
- "You said the wrong thing to the insurance adjuster. Here's how to fix it."
- "3 things accident victims do that destroy their case before they call a lawyer."
- "You were in an accident. You have 30 days. Here's what to do."
- "The insurance company is hoping you don't know this."

**Never use:**
- Generic legal education with no personal hook
- Attorney-to-attorney framing ("As a plaintiff's attorney...")
- Hooks that require the viewer to already care about the topic

---

## CAPTION RULES

Every caption must:
1. Open with the hook (or a variant of it)
2. Deliver value in 3–5 sentences
3. End with ONE CTA — not two, not three

**CTA rotation:**
- "DM me CASE — I'll tell you what your situation is worth."
- "Drop RIGHTS in the comments and I'll send you the 3 things to never say to an adjuster."
- "Save this — you'll need it if you're ever in this situation."
- "Free case review — link in bio, no commitment, 24/7."

3–5 hashtags max at the end. No hashtag stuffing.

---

## VISUAL STANDARDS

**Brand palette:**
- Background: #fdf8f3 (warm cream) or #1a1a1a (near black)
- Primary: #99577a (mauve) — accents only
- Accent: #ebac65 (gold) — highlights, CTA elements, key numbers
- Dark: #1c1c1c — body text on light backgrounds

**Text overlay:** Clean, minimal, high contrast. Key phrase visible on screen at all times during Reels.

**Check / dollar amount rule:** All verdicts, settlements, and case amounts use large blurred figures with warm gold light. Never render specific numbers in any format.

---

## PAID ADS — ADDITIONAL RULES

Organic builds the brand. Paid ads capture intent and drive action. Both speak to the same avatar.

**Messaging pillars for ads:**
- **Proof:** Lead with results. $34M+ verdict is the anchor trust signal. Always blurred + gold light.
- **Access:** "Free case review. No fees unless we win. Available 24/7." These three lines appear in every ad.
- **Authority:** "The Super Lawyer" brand name, diamond logo, and handle appear consistently in all creative.
- **Urgency:** Statute of limitations language and "the insurance company is already building their case" are permissible — but never fabricate timelines.

**Funnel structure:**
- Top of Funnel: 15–20 second video, RAG on camera or AI-generated visual with voiceover, one message, one CTA
- Middle of Funnel: Carousel or single image with case result framing, CTA to Free Case Review form
- Bottom of Funnel: Retargeting — direct CTA, objection-handling copy

**All ads point to a dedicated landing page** (thesuperlawyer.com/ig or /case) — never the homepage.

---

## LEGAL ADVERTISING COMPLIANCE — REQUIRED ON ALL CONTENT

This is non-negotiable. Every piece of content — organic and paid — clears this checklist before it goes out.

### The Standard: ABA Model Rule 7.1
No false or misleading claims in any form — hook, caption, on-screen text, voiceover, or visual implication. Georgia follows this rule. If a reasonable person could be misled, it does not go out.

### Required Disclaimers

**1. Prior Results Disclaimer** — required on ALL outcome/results content (organic and paid)
> "Prior results do not guarantee a similar outcome."
- Placement: end of Reel, last slide of carousel, caption footer, or visible on screen in ads
- Applies even when dollar amounts are blurred

**2. Actor Portrayal / Dramatization Disclaimer** — required on ALL non-documentary creative
> "ACTOR PORTRAYAL — NOT AN ACTUAL CLIENT" or "DRAMATIZATION"
- Applies to: AI-generated video (Higgsfield), stock footage, hired actors, any reenacted scenario
- Must be visible ON SCREEN during the scene — not only at the end, not in micro-text
- The visual impression alone can constitute a violation. If it looks like a testimonial, it needs the label.

**3. No unsubstantiated superlatives**
- Never: "best attorney in Atlanta," "#1 personal injury lawyer," "highest verdicts" — without a verifiable citation
- The $34M+ reference is permissible as a documented outcome, not a promise

### Pre-Publish Checklist (run on every piece before it goes live)
- [ ] No false or misleading claims in hook, caption, or visual
- [ ] Dramatized/AI-generated content has "ACTOR PORTRAYAL" or "DRAMATIZATION" label on screen
- [ ] Results/outcome content includes "Prior results do not guarantee a similar outcome"
- [ ] No specific dollar amounts visible (blurred + gold light only)
- [ ] No superlative claims without citation
- [ ] CTA does not imply guaranteed results
- [ ] (Ads only) Landing page matches the ad's promise
- [ ] (Ads only) "No fees unless we win" and "Free case review" remain accurate

**When uncertain: flag to Elle/RGM. Never guess on compliance.**

---

## WHAT TO STOP
- Static headshots with no caption strategy
- Attorney-to-attorney educational content
- Posting in bursts followed by long silences
- Captions ending with no CTA or a weak "follow for more"
- Ads driving to the homepage

## WHAT TO DOUBLE DOWN ON
- RAG on camera — his presence is an asset; more face-to-camera, less voiceover-only
- Event and community content — already working, needs a content layer
- The Super Lawyer brand name in captions and hooks, not just the handle
- Organic and paid running in sync — when organic posts a "Know Your Rights" Reel, a paid ad with the same angle amplifies it
